--- title: "🗓️ Session 8: Data visualization" date: "2026-11-13" date-modified: last-modified --- One area for which R is particulary well-known for is the area of *visualization*. This is particularly because of the package [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/). This session introduces `ggplot2` and the general approach to generate visualization in R. The good thing is that if you follow the approach described here, you can basically create every visualization type you can think of. ## 👨‍🏫 Lecture Slides [**Download the slides of this session**](/content/material/slides/E7-Visualization.pdf) (PDF) ## 🎥 Lecture videos All the videos are available via this [playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZDawQMrG1RL_OhYImHUM-F9rHsizLxYx&si=ofMKoYwusOS38sZL). ```{=html}
``` ## 📚 Mandatory Reading - The tutorial [visualization](/content/tutorials/visualization/index.qmd) ## Further Reading - @hadleygraphics, who introduces the theory underlying `ggplot2` - [ggplot2 cheat sheet](https://github.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/blob/main/data-visualization.pdf) - Browse the website [from Data to Viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/) and try to re-create some of the figures yourself - I like this [blog](https://blog.yan-holtz.com) from Yan Holtz, the creator of [from Data to Viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/); it helps highlighting the relevance of often under-appreciated aspects of a graph, such as its [title](https://blog.yan-holtz.com/posts/the-neglected-detail) ## ✍️ Coursework - Do the exercises `Visualization1` from the `DataScienceExercises` package ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Quick code for starting the exercises ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} learnr::run_tutorial( name = "Visualization1", package = "DataScienceExercises", shiny_args=list("launch.browser"=TRUE)) ``` ::: :::
